An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 26.2
div.ab: Qui, si nimis confidens in pace quam habet, per superbiam alicui forisfecerit, damnum restauret et iterum tantumdem, quod Angli uocant forisfacturam a[f]trikelt [b]et[e].
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 650 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: But if, trusting too much in the peace that he has, he commits an offence against anyone through pride, let him make good the damage and as much again, which the English call the fine a[f]trikelt [b]et[e] (repayment-compensation).
